channel.description: Recent content in AI on Archit's Space

item.title: Self-Improving AI Agents: A Recursive Taxonomy
item.description: Six families of self-improving AI agent, 109 methods, ranked: what each one changes about itself, how durable that change is, and the handful that matter.

item.title: Memori: The Recursive Design of Agent Memory
item.description: Agent memory is a retrieval problem, not a storage one. Why memory is really three problems—and why Memori stores rules about how to use itself.

item.title: Building Persistent Memory for AI Agents: Architecture Decisions in Memori
item.description: The engineering behind Memori, a persistent memory system for AI coding agents: hybrid RRF search, access-decay scoring, and cosine deduplication.

item.title: Hard Constraints Belong in Code: The Probabilistic-Deterministic Hybrid Agent Pattern
item.description: LLMs explore solution spaces; deterministic code guarantees correctness. High-stakes architecture wires both: model priors to explore, code to enforce.

item.title: Designing CLI Tools for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Memori
item.description: Designing command-line tools AI coding agents can actually use: output modes, error design, behavioral snippets, and making machines help themselves.

item.title: The AI-Augmented Developer Playbook: Architect, Delegate, Validate
item.description: Shifting from code-producing craftsman to AI-orchestrating architect: abstract thinking, pattern libraries, and rigorous validation for higher leverage.

item.title: Forging AI’s Lasting Memory: Lessons from Asimov and First Principles
item.description: Why modern AI agents forget, how Asimov's positronic robots managed memory, and a first-principles guide to memory that endures across sessions.
